steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named 'InteractionTest' that returns an empty React fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name 'InteractionTest' that returns an empty fragment.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the InteractionTest component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a component named InteractionTest that returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named 'InteractionTest' is defined and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named 'InteractionTest' that returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function named 'InteractionTest' and it returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize state for click count
steps.instruction: Inside the InteractionTest component, declare a state variable named 'clickCount' with an initial value of 0 using the useState hook.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [clickCount, setClickCount] = useState(0);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: declaring a state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a clickCount state variable initialized to 0, ready to track button clicks.
successCriteria: A clickCount state variable is declared with useState, initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to track button clicks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clickCount state wasn't properly initialized. Check the useState syntax.

steps.title: Initialize state for input value
steps.instruction: Inside your InteractionTest component, declare a state variable named 'inputValue' with an initial value of an empty string using useState.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook to create another state variable. The syntax is similar to the clickCount state you already have.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another state variable for text
const [text, setText] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: clickCount for tracking clicks and inputValue for tracking text input.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string using useState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a second state variable to track text input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to declare a variable named 'inputValue' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires declaring a state variable named 'inputValue' with an initial value of an empty string using useState. Check your syntax.

steps.title: Define click handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your InteractionTest component, define a function named handleClick that increments the clickCount state by 1.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setClickCount with the current clickCount plus 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleClick function is defined that increases clickCount by 1 when called.
successCriteria: The handleClick function is defined and uses setClickCount to increment clickCount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the click handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it increments clickCount by 1 using setClickCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleClick function is not defined or doesn't increment clickCount correctly.

steps.title: Define input change handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named 'handleInputChange' inside your component that updates the inputValue state with the event target value.
steps.hint: Create a function that takes an event parameter and calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleInputChange function is defined and ready to be used with an input element.
successCriteria: A function named handleInputChange is defined inside the component that calls setInputValue with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the input change handler function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function takes an event parameter and updates inputValue state using setInputValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name and that it updates the inputValue state.

steps.title: Add main container structure
steps.instruction: In your InteractionTest component, return a div container with a heading that says 'Test User Interactions'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div containing an h1 element with the text 'Test User Interactions'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a basic structure with a heading inside a div container.
successCriteria: The component returns a div containing an h1 element with the text 'Test User Interactions'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the main container structure with the correct heading.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a div containing an h1 with exactly 'Test User Interactions' as the text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match what was requested. Please ensure you return a div with an h1 containing 'Test User Interactions'.

steps.title: Add click counter display
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current clickCount value.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to create a

element with the clickCount state variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current click count value in a paragraph element.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays the clickCount state value using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully displayed the clickCount state in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using a paragraph element and displaying the clickCount variable inside curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element with the clickCount value is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add button with click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Click me' and wire its onClick event to the handleClick function.
steps.hint: Place the button inside the main container div, after the paragraph. Use the onClick attribute to call your handler function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an interactive button
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a button labeled 'Click me' that increments the click counter when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Click me' is added, and its onClick attribute is set to call handleClick.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an interactive button that will trigger the click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct text and the onClick is wired to handleClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected to the click handler. Check the syntax and placement.

steps.title: Add input with change handler
steps.instruction: Add an input field and a paragraph showing inputValue, then wire the input's onChange event to the handleInputChange function.
steps.hint:
Add an element with value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange}, then add a

element that displays the current inputValue.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a functional input field that updates the inputValue state when typed into, and a paragraph that displays the current input value.
successCriteria: An input element with value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange} is added, and a paragraph element displaying inputValue is present.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an interactive input field and displayed its value. The input now updates the state and shows the current value in real-time.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the input field with value and onChange attributes, and a paragraph that displays inputValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field or paragraph showing inputValue is missing or incorrectly implemented. Check that you've added both elements and wired the onChange event properly.
